newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, advisers discuss NATO, Europe.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, advisers discuss NATO, Europe.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and his foreign policy advisers held talks on Thursday on his second-term objectives toward expanding NATO and other issues facing Europe.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said it was the first in a series of foreign policy meetings Clinton will hold in coming weeks on his plans for his second term. The group heard a report from Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott, who returned on Wednesday night from a tour of European capitals to discuss NATO.

Clinton and his top aides have identified six strategic global priorities for his second term and at the top of the list was how to make Europe an undivided continent at peace from London to the Urals.

U.S. and European leaders are currently debating how to expand NATO to accept some former members of the Soviet empire without damaging relations with the Russian Federation, which strongly opposes expansion of the Western alliance.

A NATO summit is planned for July in Madrid to issue invitations to certain countries, so far unidentified, to apply for NATO membership. NATO diplomats are also working with Russia on a new charter to serve as the blueprint of the alliance's future partnership with Moscow.
